title: Blind pianist Rosebud and Clarence Williams at Big Du Bois
summary: A blind teacher, Rosebud, played piano at Big Du Bois's tonk, near Howard Avenue; Dick asks about his era.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. a blind teacher called Rosebud, and he used to play at Big Du Bois, Calvary. Well, he was playing piano and I was playing piano.
Was he a guy around Clarence Williams age?
That's what I'm talking about. Clarence Williams. Mm-hmm. Clarence Williams, yeah. A school-based Clarence.
Yeah.
And did you play with him at Big Du Bois? Big Du Bois.
Where was that?
That's right at, at Howard Avenue Ramport. Do you ever pass and see the sign, the sign, the place called the Sunset?
Howard Avenue in Ramport?
Yeah, right on that park home.
On the downtown side?
Yeah.
I don't guess I know that. I can't place it.
Well, that was the Big Du Bois.
Mm-hmm. Was that a tonk? Oh, a tonk.
Mm-hmm.
I guess they had a lot of his own numbers then, huh? Oh, yeah. I know he wrote some good ones. Yeah, he wrote some good ones. Do you remember any of the ones he featured in?
No, I couldn't.
I like his stuff.
He's a good player too. Mm-hmm.
He must not have been too old, because he left you a long time ago. Oh, yeah.
He left you a long time ago. Oh, yeah. He left you a long time ago. Mm-hmm. Was that before World War I or after?
Before World War I or after? Before World War I. Was it before the big storm or after that? Before the storm. Before the...
No, during the storm. During the storm? Mm-hmm.
That'd be about 1950.
Yeah, about 1950.
Because that's when the storm was.
When he did travel. Yeah.
